## Literature Review

This section should present a review of the **5 required scientific articles**.
These articles should be recent (publication date between **2019 and 2026**) and
relevant within the course project themes.

---

## Title of Project Idea #1

This section should present an introduction, background and objective of the
first proposed project idea. One of the scientific articles reviewed should
support the idea.

This section should also provide a clear statement of the research issue under
investigation (the research question) and provide some justification of the need
for research to be conducted on this topic (e.g. if the research will meet a need
or deliver productive outcomes for a certain field/practice).

You may use subsections provided in the template as well. For example, see below.

### Selecting a Template

This template has been tailored for output on the A4 paper size. Do not alter
margins, column widths, line spaces, or font specifications.

### Units

- Use either SI (MKS) or CGS as primary units. SI is encouraged.
- Avoid combining SI and CGS units.
- Clearly state the units for each quantity used in an equation.

**Keywords** — robotics, multi-agent, cooperative, meta-heuristics, optimization

## References

Number citations consecutively within brackets `[1]`. The sentence punctuation
follows the bracket `[2]`. Refer simply to the reference number, as in `[3]` — do
not use "Ref. [3]" or "reference [3]" except at the beginning of a sentence:
"Reference [3] was the first ...".

- Give all authors' names unless there are six or more (then "et al." is allowed).
- Unpublished papers: cite as "unpublished".
- Accepted papers: cite as "in press".
- Capitalize only the first word in a paper title, except for proper nouns and
  element symbols.
- For translated journals, give the English citation first, then the original.

### Reference formatting examples

1. G. Eason, B. Noble, and I. N. Sneddon, "On certain integrals of
   Lipschitz-Hankel type involving products of Bessel functions," _Phil. Trans.
   Roy. Soc. London_, vol. A247, pp. 529–551, April 1955.
2. J. Clerk Maxwell, _A Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism_, 3rd ed., vol. 2.
   Oxford: Clarendon, 1892, pp. 68–73.
3. I. S. Jacobs and C. P. Bean, "Fine particles, thin films and exchange
   anisotropy," in _Magnetism_, vol. III, G. T. Rado and J. A. Suhl, Eds. New
   York: Academic, 1963, pp. 271–350.
